source.title: On Neural Networks Fitting, Compression, and Generalization Behavior via Information-Bottleneck-like Approaches
source.authors: Zhaoyang Lyu; Gholamali Aminian; M. Rodrigues

record.tranche_reason: The study uses estimated input-reconstruction and label cross-entropy measures to examine training dynamics and generalization across architectures, optimizers, and regularization settings; it does not use the original claim’s random-label or sharpness tests.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on generalization across optimizers and dropout settings. Its compression measures are not the magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness named in V7. It does not test arbitrary-label memorization or generalization beyond the interpolation threshold.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out loss and accuracy across optimizers and dropout rates, bearing on V4 and V6. Its tabulated GE is a test-minus-training loss gap, so GE alone cannot establish either version's held-out performance effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors report fitting and compression across the tested activation functions and associate stronger fitting/compression with better generalization across architectures, algorithms, and datasets. They specifically report adaptive optimizers outperforming non-adaptive ones and regularization helping in suitable configurations. They present the compression–generalization connection as a conjectural association, not an established causal explanation.
record.recipe_differences: The study tracks input-reconstruction MMSE proxies and label cross-entropy during training; it does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, or magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported generalization outcomes vary with optimizer, dropout rate, architecture, kernel count and size, and dataset. Estimator depth can affect measure values, though the authors report similar trends across tested estimator depths.

fits_no_version.finding: Wider four-layer MNIST MLPs have progressively lower test losses, but zero training error and post-interpolation widening are not established.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width affects held-out performance and reconstruction-based compression dynamics in these four-layer MLPs.

fits_no_version.finding: CNN kernel count and size affect held-out performance and measured compression; larger loss gaps sometimes accompany better held-out performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CNN architectural choices affect held-out performance and representation dynamics in this CIFAR-10 setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Models trained on the CIFAR-10 subset, full CIFAR-10, and CINIC have different held-out performance and compression dynamics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-data amount and composition are associated with generalization and reconstruction-based compression.

record.problems: The study uses proxy measures rather than direct information quantities and generalization-gap sharpness. It does not report uncertainty for the tabulated generalization values. Some table values appear difficult to reconcile with prose descriptions, including CNN dropout 30% and kernel-count comparisons; results are limited to the tested datasets and architectures.
record.rows_left_out: No separately tabulated rows for training loss, test loss, or train/test accuracy were extracted; the GE metric and explicit prose comparisons were retained for the relevant optimizer and dropout claims. Architecture and dataset findings outside the listed versions are summarized under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level random-label held-out performance alongside natural-label generalization.
Widening beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold in the specified network setting.
CNN versus fully connected classifiers on the same image task; learned local connectivity and convolution-derived initialization.
Optimizer-specific learning-rate and schedule tuning, broader tuning, language tasks, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Standalone fully connected classifiers, very small training sets, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after memorization-based versus random example removal.

missing.what: Direct held-out optimizer outcomes and accompanying training outcomes are needed to substantiate V4. Although rows_left_out declares their omission, R1–R4 currently retain only loss gaps; add the Table 4 test-loss and accuracy columns used in the verdict.

Direct dropout test-loss and accuracy outcomes, plus training loss for the excessive-dropout condition, are needed. Their declared omission leaves R5–R8 unable to establish V6 from GE alone, and reverses the apparent conclusion at 30% dropout.

record.verdict_notes: All tabulated GE values represent test-minus-training loss gaps, subject to rounding. Their numerical values are generally extracted correctly, but interpreting them as held-out error creates incorrect verdicts. States for R1–R8 therefore remain cannot_determine for their current measures; verdicts explicitly use the supplied tables' direct outcomes. The optimizer table's approximately 99% test accuracies differ markedly from other nominally similar CNN/CIFAR-10 tables; the supplied text does not explain this discrepancy. No uncertainty establishes statistical significance.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same recipes.
Whether test error keeps falling after zero training error or peaks near the interpolation threshold.
CNN versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and learned or transferred connectivity.
Language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models.
Batch-size comparisons and fixed-epoch large-batch training.
Fully connected classifiers, very small training sets, and removing dropout and weight decay together with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and comparing with random-example removal.

rows.subject: CNN SGD
rows.operation_detail: Train CNN on CIFAR-10 using SGD; learning rate 0.001.
rows.note: Compared with adaptive optimizers in the same experiment; this value alone does not establish the version’s expected direction.
rows.check: 0.0226 is the reported loss gap, not held-out error. Retain as a comparator, but use Table 4 test loss 0.0429 and test accuracy 0.9882 for V4.

rows.subject: CNN SGD-momentum
rows.operation_detail: Train CNN on CIFAR-10 using SGD-momentum; learning rate 0.001 and momentum 0.9.
rows.note: Compared with adaptive optimizers in the same experiment.
rows.check: 0.0226 is the loss gap. The relevant comparator outcomes are test loss 0.0356 and test accuracy 0.9882.

rows.subject: CNN Adam
rows.operation_detail: Train CNN on CIFAR-10 using Adam; learning rate 0.001.
rows.note: Adam has lower GE than either SGD or SGD-momentum in this experiment.
rows.check: The recorded gap cannot establish better held-out performance. Replace or supplement it with test loss 0.0275 and test accuracy 0.9896; these reverse V4's adaptive-method disadvantage relative to R1 and R2.

rows.subject: CNN RMSproop
rows.operation_detail: Train CNN on CIFAR-10 using RMSprop; learning rate 0.001.
rows.note: The table spells the model condition as “RMSproop”; the text identifies RMSprop. It has the lowest GE among the listed optimizers.
rows.check: Normalize the subject spelling to RMSprop. Replace or supplement the gap with test loss 0.0263 and test accuracy 0.9908; these reverse the adaptive-method disadvantage relative to R1 and R2.

rows.subject: CNN 0% dropout
rows.operation_detail: Train CNN on CIFAR-10 without dropout.
rows.note: No-dropout reference for the tested dropout rates.
rows.check: 0.1553 is the loss gap. The no-dropout reference needed for V6 is test loss 0.8300 and test accuracy 0.7190.

rows.subject: CNN 30% dropout
rows.operation_detail: Train CNN with dropout in the first fully connected layer.
rows.note: Although the prose says low dropout had more compression, this table reports higher GE than the no-dropout condition.
rows.check: The reversed state incorrectly treats a larger loss gap as worse held-out performance. Test loss falls from 0.8300 to 0.7985 and test accuracy rises from 0.7190 to 0.7398, supporting the dropout benefit.

rows.subject: CNN 60% dropout
rows.operation_detail: Train CNN with dropout in the first fully connected layer.
rows.note: The authors identify this as the best generalization performance among the tested dropout conditions.
rows.check: The recorded gap alone cannot show V6. Test loss 0.7606 versus 0.8300 and test accuracy 0.7510 versus 0.7190 directly establish the dropout benefit.

rows.subject: CNN 90% dropout
rows.operation_detail: Train CNN with dropout in the first fully connected layer.
rows.note: Higher GE than the no-dropout condition; the text also reports less pronounced fitting and compression at this high rate.
rows.check: Use test loss 0.8765 versus 0.8300 and test accuracy 0.7000 versus 0.7190 to establish worse held-out performance. Training loss also rises to 1.0768 from 0.6747, consistent with V6's excessive-dropout underfitting qualification.

rows.subject: MLP 16 × 4
rows.operation_detail: Compare four-layer MLP widths trained on MNIST with SGD at learning rate 0.001.
rows.note: The width sweep reports generalization alongside fitting and compression dynamics but does not test the interpolation-threshold claim.
rows.check: GE is a loss gap. This width comparison does not establish zero training error or widening beyond interpolation.

rows.subject: MLP 64 × 4
rows.operation_detail: Compare four-layer MLP widths trained on MNIST with SGD at learning rate 0.001.
rows.note: The width sweep reports generalization alongside fitting and compression dynamics but does not test the interpolation-threshold claim.
rows.check: GE is a loss gap; the interpolation condition required by V2 is unestablished.

rows.subject: MLP 512 × 4
rows.operation_detail: Compare four-layer MLP widths trained on MNIST with SGD at learning rate 0.001.
rows.note: The widest tested MLP has the best GE in this width comparison; zero training error and an interpolation threshold are not tested.
rows.check: The widest network has the lowest test loss, but its training accuracy is 0.9967 rather than perfect; V2's post-interpolation comparison is not established.

rows.subject: CNN baseline
rows.operation_detail: Train baseline CNN architecture on CIFAR-10 with Adam; vary kernel count relative to baseline.
rows.note: Used as the reference condition for the kernel-count sweep.
rows.check: A kernel-count reference within one CNN family does not test a listed version; GE is a loss gap.

rows.subject: CNN ×2
rows.operation_detail: Double the number of kernels in each convolutional layer; train with Adam on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: The table reports a higher GE than baseline, while the text describes test-loss performance as similar.
rows.check: Remove the reversed state. The larger gap does not imply worse held-out performance: test loss is 0.8303 versus 0.8300, while test accuracy improves to 0.7514 from 0.7190.

rows.subject: CNN ×4
rows.size_stated: four times baseline number of kernels
rows.operation_detail: Multiply the number of kernels in each convolutional layer by four; train with Adam on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: The table reports a higher GE than baseline; the text says the test loss and generalization performance are similar.
rows.check: Remove the reversed state. Despite the larger gap, test loss improves to 0.7801 from 0.8300 and test accuracy to 0.7332 from 0.7190.

rows.subject: CNN /2
rows.operation_detail: Halve the number of kernels in each convolutional layer; train with Adam on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: The table reports a higher GE than baseline.
rows.check: No listed version is tested. Held-out loss is 0.9055 versus 0.8300; the recorded GE measures the loss gap.

rows.subject: CNN /4
rows.size_stated: one quarter baseline number of kernels
rows.operation_detail: Reduce the number of kernels in each convolutional layer to one quarter; train with Adam on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: The table reports a higher GE than baseline.
rows.check: No listed version is tested. Held-out loss is 1.0494 versus 0.8300; the recorded GE measures the loss gap.

rows.subject: CNN /8
rows.size_stated: one eighth baseline number of kernels
rows.operation_detail: Reduce the number of kernels in each convolutional layer to one eighth; train with Adam on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: The table reports higher GE than baseline but the smallest GE among reduced-kernel conditions.
rows.check: The smallest gap among reduced-kernel models does not mean best held-out performance: this group has the worst test loss, 1.1353.

rows.subject: CNN 1 × 1
rows.operation_detail: Use 1 × 1 kernels in all convolutional layers; train with Adam on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: The 3 × 3 model is reported as having the best test loss and generalization performance.
rows.check: Kernel-size comparisons within CNNs do not test V3. The GE value is the loss gap; test loss is 1.1860 versus 0.8065 for 3 × 3 kernels.

rows.subject: CNN 3 × 3
rows.operation_detail: Use baseline 3 × 3 kernels in all convolutional layers; train with Adam on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: Best GE among the listed kernel sizes.
rows.check: No fully connected comparator is present. Table 3 reports test loss 0.8065 here but 0.8300 for the nominally equivalent baseline elsewhere; preserve that source discrepancy.

rows.subject: CNN 5 × 5
rows.operation_detail: Use 5 × 5 kernels in all convolutional layers; train with Adam on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: The 3 × 3 model is reported as having the best test loss and generalization performance.
rows.check: Remove the version-relative reversed state; this within-CNN kernel-size comparison fits no version.

rows.subject: CNN 7 × 7
rows.operation_detail: Use 7 × 7 kernels in all convolutional layers; train with Adam on CIFAR-10.
rows.note: The 3 × 3 model is reported as having the best test loss and generalization performance.
rows.check: Remove the version-relative reversed state; this within-CNN kernel-size comparison fits no version.

rows.subject: CNN 1% CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Train CNN with Adam on 1% of CIFAR-10.
rows.note: The authors report this smallest-dataset model has the worst generalization performance.
rows.check: Dataset-size variation without dropout or memorization-based removal tests neither V6 nor V8. GE is a loss gap.

rows.subject: CNN 100% CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Train CNN with Adam on full CIFAR-10.
rows.note: Full CIFAR-10 reference for the dataset-size comparison.
rows.check: This dataset-size reference does not test a listed version.

rows.subject: CNN CINIC
rows.operation_detail: Train CNN with Adam on CINIC.
rows.note: The authors report this model has the best generalization performance in the dataset comparison.
rows.check: CINIC changes dataset composition as well as sample count; this is not an isolated sample-size effect or a test of a listed version.

relationships.condition: Reported CNN optimizer comparison, identified as CIFAR-10, with learning rate fixed at 0.001 for every optimizer
relationships.reason: Table 4's held-out outcomes associated with R1–R4 show Adam/RMSprop test losses of 0.0275/0.0263 versus SGD/momentum's 0.0429/0.0356. This local reversal uses the text's test-loss columns, not the recorded GE gaps, and does not establish results under optimizer-specific tuning.
relationships.display_finding: Adam and RMSprop reportedly had lower test losses than SGD and momentum SGD at the shared learning rate, but these comparisons remain unverified.
